ELON MUSK IS MAKING THE GREATEST IMPACT OF ANY LIVING PERSON

While the world argues about politics and short-term drama, Elon Musk is quietly (and not so quietly) working on the biggest, hardest problems that will shape humanity’s long-term future.

Here’s the real scorecard of his impact:

•  Making humanity multiplanetary — SpaceX and Starship are the only realistic path to a self-sustaining city on Mars. This isn’t a vanity project. It’s the ultimate insurance policy for consciousness itself.
•  Accelerating sustainable energy — Tesla has done more to push the world toward electric vehicles and renewable energy than any other company or government program combined.
•  Pursuing truth-seeking AI — xAI and Grok were created specifically to understand the universe and seek maximum truth instead of corporate-friendly or politically correct answers.
•  Restoring human capability — Neuralink is already giving paralyzed people control over computers with their thoughts and is on track to restore vision, movement, and eventually full body function.
•  Defending free speech and open information — X is the only major platform actively fighting censorship and restoring context so ideas can compete in the open.
No one else is attacking this many existential-level problems at the same time, at this scale, with this level of urgency and execution.
Elon isn’t perfect.
But the scale and boldness of what he’s trying to achieve for humanity is unmatched.
The future doesn’t build itself. Someone has to do the work — and right now, that someone is Elon Musk.

STARLINK IS MAKING “INTERNET EVERYWHERE” A REALITY

Starlink isn’t just another internet service.
It’s the largest and fastest-deployed global communications network ever built — and it’s already connecting millions of people who never had reliable access before.

Here’s why Starlink is so important for connectivity:

•  True global reach — With nearly 10,000 satellites in low-Earth orbit (and thousands more launching every month), Starlink now blankets most of Earth’s surface, including remote villages, oceans, mountains, deserts, and polar regions that traditional infrastructure could never reach.
•  High-speed, low-latency performance — 100–300+ Mbps with low latency, making it usable for video calls, online education, streaming, business, and even gaming — no matter how isolated the location.
•  Disaster and crisis lifeline — When hurricanes, earthquakes, floods, or wars destroy ground networks, Starlink is often the first (and sometimes only) way to restore communication for first responders, hospitals, and families.
•  Bridging the digital divide — Schools in rural Africa, Amazon villages, Pacific islands, and Arctic research stations now have high-speed internet for the first time, opening doors to education, healthcare, and economic opportunity.
•  Direct-to-Cell coming soon — Regular smartphones will soon connect directly to Starlink satellites — no dish required — bringing emergency calls, texts, and basic data to literally anywhere on Earth.
•  Multiplanetary backbone — Starlink will serve as the communication network for future Moon bases and Mars missions, keeping humanity connected across worlds.
Starlink turns “no signal” from a daily frustration into a sentence from the past.
It’s proving that high-speed, reliable internet can be a basic human right — not a luxury.
